title: The Implications of a Maritime Blockade on Energy Poverty in Israel
abstract: In recent decades, the global energy system has become more vulnerable to disruptions due to geopolitical events. The increasing dependence on maritime shipping lanes or energy infrastructure located at sea increases the risk of blockades and associated economic crises. A maritime blockade, even if temporary, may disrupt the supply of primary energy sources, cause sharp increases in energy prices, and exacerbate social gaps through the expansion of energy poverty – a situation in which households are forced to devote an unreasonable portion of their income to basic energy consumption. This study examined the economic impact of a maritime blockade on the Israeli energy economy, focusing on the electricity sector as a key indicator of household well-being. The analysis is based on historical data from the Israel Electric Corporation on consumption and price, combined with simulations of scenarios of blockages in the supply of Israeli natural gas and distillates (products produced in the refining process from crude oil) arriving via sea supply routes. The findings indicate that a complete blockage of the supply of natural gas causes an increase of approximately 28% in electricity prices, and almost triples the rate of households exceeding the energy poverty line in the event that the gas rigs are unavailable. This damage will require massive investment from the state treasury to keep all households in the country above the energy poverty line. These findings indicate a direct link between energy vulnerability due to a sea blockade and socio-economic stability, and emphasize the importance of advanced energy policy and public welfare infrastructure as complementary infrastructures for national security in an era of energy risks. Global.
summary: A maritime blockade could disrupt energy supplies that reach Israel by sea, raising prices and pushing more households into energy poverty, where basic energy takes an unreasonable share of income. We combined historical Israel Electric Corporation data on consumption and prices with simulated blockades of natural gas and distillate supplies. A complete blockage of natural gas causes an increase of approximately 28% in electricity prices and almost triples the rate of households exceeding the energy poverty line if the gas rigs are unavailable.
